question: Does a second `open` on an already-opened circuit charge FEE() again?
answer: No. The second call reverts and costs only gas (~0.000056 OKB). It does not take the 0.08 OKB opener fee a second time.

method.how: Impersonated the circuit holder on the fork (anvil_impersonateAccount + anvil_setBalance), sent the real opener.open(processor, tokenId) call with value = FEE(), mined a block, and read the receipt plus the holder's balance delta.
method.command: PATH="$HOME/.foundry/bin:$PATH" node .corepack/v1/pnpm/9.15.4/bin/pnpm.cjs exec vitest run tests/fork/second-open.test.ts

consequence: A repeat open is not a double-charge vector on chain, so the DB single-live-intent index is defence in depth rather than the only protection.
It is still not free: a user who retries pays gas each time, so the UI must not invite a retry while a send is unresolved.
The revert reason is opaque from this measurement; the product must not promise a specific error message for a repeat open.
notProven: No mainnet transaction was sent; this is a local fork of one pinned block.
Behaviour after a state change on the circuit (transfer, or a protocol upgrade) is unmeasured.
The exact revert selector is unknown because the receipt carries no revert data.
